title: FOUR COMMANDS, ONE EVIDENCE PATH
question: Which Eval Evidence command should I run, what does it produce, and what does that result prove?
takeaway: Practice with demo, inspect without writing with check, create a portable baseline with bundle, and re-check retained bytes with verify --run-root.

reading_speeds.at_2_seconds: Four commands lead to four visibly different outputs along one evidence path.
reading_speeds.at_20_seconds: Each row maps a command through its action to a named artifact or result.
reading_speeds.at_2_minutes: Each output is paired with an explicit proof limit, source mapping, edge meaning, accessibility contract, and render provenance.

medium.rationale: Exact command syntax, distinct output geometry, accessible text, and auditable proof boundaries must survive code review.

labels.claim: Writes deterministic synthetic practice input; it is not real-run evidence.
Detects and validates a run in memory and re-hashes references, producing a pass/fail report but no stored baseline.
Validates and writes canonical evidence JSON that binds claims to referenced digests but does not authenticate a signer.
Validates the bundle and re-hashes retained source bytes, reporting match or mismatch without establishing physical truth.
Output of verify with a run root.
Every command result is paired with an explicit adjacent proof limit.
The first column names exact CLI commands.
The second column summarizes the sourced command action.
The third column names the distinct artifact or report produced by the command.
The final column distinguishes supported facts from adjacent unsupported claims.
Names the scoped fact established by the command path.
Summarizes the three command-level limitations that must survive at full size.
Demo appears first as the recommended learning entry point.
Check follows as the read-only validation path.
Bundle follows as the stored-baseline path.
Verify with run root follows as the retained-byte comparison path.

boundaries: check is read-only and does not create the later baseline.
verify without --run-root checks schema and embedded digest only; it does not re-hash source files.
Digests show scoped byte identity, not who created the evidence or whether a reported result is physically true.
forbidden_claims: Do not label any command result authenticated, certified, or physically verified.
Do not claim model ranking or production readiness.
Do not present the recommended learning order as a required runtime dependency.

accessibility.alt_text: Demo creates practice input, check reports without storing a baseline, bundle writes a canonical baseline, and verify with run root compares retained bytes.
accessibility.long_description: Four rows form a command switchboard. Demo materializes deterministic example files. Check detects, validates, and re-hashes references in memory. Bundle validates and writes canonical evidence JSON. Verify with run root validates the bundle and re-hashes retained source bytes. Each row names its output and a fact the command does not prove.
color_independent_cues: explicit PROVES and DOES NOT PROVE text
